thread:
Maria R.: heads-up — onboarding a quantized Llama-variant (int4, group=128) and saw a flaky context divergence with long system prompts + streaming chunking. got a small repro, curious if anyone's seen prefix replay/shadowing before.
Ashwin P.: can you paste the minimal repro and the exact symptoms? is this looking like a KV-cache index mismatch or tokenization drift?
Maria R.: minimal steps below. behavior: generation looks fine until ~token 7.8k, then the model emits a short repeated segment from ~token 2.5k (older prefix) and continues as if key indices shifted. not a standard hallucination.
Maria R.: repro (pseudo):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rwl-llama-q4",
  "system_prompt": "<4096-token system blob>",
  "input": "<streamed user chunks totaling ~2048 tokens>",
  "stream_chunk_size": 512,
  "kv_offload_threshold": "8GB",
  "stream_backpressure": true
}
```
Maria R.: sample log excerpt:
```
[00:12:34] kv_index=12567 allocated
[00:12:35] prefill stream chunk=512 -> offload triggered
[00:12:36] kv_index shrink: 12567 -> 6289 (partial shard offloaded)
[00:12:36] gen_pos=7811 emitted="...old-prefix-segment..."
```
Kevin L.: interesting — looks like a partial offload is leaving stale pointers that later map to earlier entries. streaming chunk boundaries + offload race could shift the base offset. which runtime version?
Maria R.: runtime 2.11.0 (kernel selection path v3). i ran a control: disable offload + stream_chunk_size=full (no streaming) -> PASS. enable offload + streaming -> FAIL consistently in my env.
Jen T.: does quantization matter? try int8?
Maria R.: int8 (q8) -> PASS. int4 -> FAIL. int4 with group_size=256 -> intermittent. int4 group_size=128 -> consistent repro.
Ashwin P.: that narrows it: int4 kernel's cache shifting during partial offload may not account for group quant granularity. can you run with KV_DEBUG=1 and dump prefill indices + physical pointer map?
Maria R.: attached small KV dump (trimmed) in logs above. KV_DEBUG shows index mismatch right after offload.
Kevin L.: plan: 1) add targeted unit reproducer in eng-ml repro harness (priming_long_system_test) 2) add kernel-level invariant assert when offload occurs to check index mapping 3) run INF nightly regression with int4 group 128. assign to @Ashwin.
Ashwin P.: ok i can take the kernel assert and repro harness. quick patch idea: ensure offload uses absolute token offsets, not relative index compressions. i'll prototype.
ci-bot: nightly-regression INF-kv-shadow-2918 queued (job id: rk-2918).
Maria R.: filing ticket https://rwd.atlassian/browse/INF-291827 (notes + reproducer + logs). i'll push the minimal reproducer to /eng-ml/repros/2918273645.md and drop results here once CI runs. thanks all :thumbsup:
Kevin L.: also add a smoke in dedicated infra (reserving small dedicated pool) to see if shard placement changes the failure mode. might be an allocator side-effect.
Maria R.: good call — i'll include dedicated-run in the ticket. leaving trace here for visibility.
